_status: Module 4, Lesson 4.3 'Sharing safely: the Traffic Light Protocol' (learner guide of 21 October 2026): TLP 2.0 labels and who may see each, plus the guide's Try it 4.3 items 3 and 4. Cases invented around the fictional RSSO.

items.text: An alert says two RSSO staff email addresses appear in a newly reported breach. May you post it in the all-staff chat?

facts.v: Your organization and its clients, on a need-to-know basis

items.reason: Ana and the two staff need it; the all-staff chat does not.

items.text: A partner office shares a list of mobile numbers used by scammers posing as the RSSO. May you post the list on the office's public Facebook page?

facts.v: Your community, such as partner offices; not the public

items.reason: To warn citizens, ask the sender's permission, or write your own warning without the list.

items.text: A public advisory on a new SMS scam. May you put it in the monthly bulletin and on the notice board?
items.reason: Share it as widely as helps.

items.text: A briefing names the RSSO in an ongoing investigation. Ana is a named recipient. May she brief her team?

facts.v: The named recipients only; no further sharing

items.reason: When in doubt, ask the sender before sharing further.

items.text: A report with no TLP label, from a vendor's security team, about your VPN product. Its sender is unclear about sharing.

facts.v: When in doubt, ask the sender before sharing further

items.reason: Remember RED, AMBER, GREEN, CLEAR: from tightest to open.
